**4. MEETING FREQUENCY AND CONVENING**

The Committee shall meet at least four times per calendar year. Additional meetings may be convened at the request of the OPS or the Committee Chair.

Meetings may be held in person, by teleconference, or by videoconference. A quorum shall consist of a majority of appointed members. Decisions of the Committee shall generally be made by consensus; where consensus cannot be reached, decisions shall be made by a simple majority of members present and voting. The Chair has a deliberative vote only.

**5. OPERATING PRINCIPLES**

In conducting its business, the Committee shall:

(a) act in good faith and in the public interest;
(b) base its advice on the best available evidence, including scientific research, incident data, and stakeholder input;
(c) declare and manage any conflicts of interest in accordance with the procedures set out in Section 7;
(d) maintain the confidentiality of commercially sensitive information and any other information marked as confidential by the OPS;
(e) support the OPS in meeting its statutory obligations under the *Competition and Consumer Act 2010* (Cth) and associated regulations.

**6. SUBCOMMITTEES AND WORKING GROUPS**

The Committee may establish subcommittees or working groups to examine specific issues in detail. Such bodies must report to the full Committee and do not have decision-making authority. The terms of reference for any subcommittee or working group shall be agreed by the Committee and recorded in the minutes.

Australian Consumer Product Safety Committee established_date 2015-03-12. Record status: current.

**7. CONFLICT OF INTEREST**

Members are required to disclose any actual, potential, or perceived conflict of interest at the commencement of each meeting agenda item where such a conflict arises. The disclosure shall be recorded in the minutes. A member with a material conflict shall withdraw from the discussion and any decision-making on the relevant item, unless otherwise determined by the Committee.

**8. SECRETARIAT AND SUPPORT**

The OPS provides secretariat support to the Committee, including the preparation of agendas, circulation of papers, and recording of minutes. The Secretariat is responsible for maintaining the Committee's records and for facilitating communication between members and the OPS.

**9. REPORTING AND ACCOUNTABILITY**

The Committee shall report to the OPS after each meeting, providing a summary of its deliberations and any recommendations. The OPS may request the Committee to provide a more detailed report on specific matters. The Committee's annual report shall be published on the OPS website.

**10. REVIEW OF THIS CHARTER**

This Charter shall be reviewed every three years, or earlier if significant changes to the Committee's role or operating environment warrant such a review. Amendments to this Charter are made by the OPS in consultation with the Committee.

**Terms of Reference and Charter**

**SECTION 11. THE CHAIRPERSON**

**11.1 Appointment**

The chairperson of the Australian Consumer Product Safety Committee is Dr. Helen Tran, as noted in the committee's terms of reference. Record status: current. Dr. Tran was appointed by the Office of Product Safety (OPS) following a nomination process open to all members of the Committee. The appointment is for a term of three years, commencing on 1 July 2022, and may be renewed by the OPS for a further term.

The OPS shall consider the following criteria when appointing the Chairperson:

- demonstrated leadership in consumer product safety or a related field;
- experience in chairing committees or similar deliberative bodies;
- impartiality and ability to manage diverse stakeholder views; and
- availability to devote sufficient time to the role.

**11.2 Duties and Responsibilities**

The Chairperson is responsible for:

a) presiding at all meetings of the Committee and ensuring that business is conducted in an orderly and efficient manner;

b) facilitating full and frank discussion among members, while ensuring that all relevant views are heard and considered;

c) ensuring that agenda items are addressed within the time allocated, or that the Committee agrees to a revised allocation;

d) ruling on points of order and procedural matters, in accordance with this Charter and any standing orders adopted by the Committee;

e) representing the Committee in its dealings with the OPS, other government agencies, and external stakeholders, except where the Committee determines that another member should represent it on a specific matter;

f) signing, on behalf of the Committee, any reports, recommendations, or correspondence approved by the Committee;

g) monitoring the implementation of the Committee's recommendations and reporting to the Committee on progress;

h) ensuring that the Committee's decisions are accurately recorded in the minutes; and

i) performing such other functions as the Committee or the OPS may from time to time determine.

**11.3 Acting Chairperson**

In the event of the Chairperson's absence or inability to act, the Deputy Chairperson shall preside. If the Deputy Chairperson is also absent, the members present shall elect one of their number to preside for that meeting. The member so elected shall have, for the duration of that meeting, all the powers and duties of the Chairperson.

**11.4 Deputy Chairperson**

The Committee shall elect a Deputy Chairperson from among its members at the first meeting following the appointment of the Chairperson. The Deputy Chairperson shall:

- act as Chairperson in the Chairperson's absence;
- assist the Chairperson in the discharge of their duties, as requested; and
- undertake such other functions as the Chairperson or the Committee may delegate.

The Deputy Chairperson shall hold office for a term of three years, or until a successor is elected.

**11.5 Removal and Resignation**

The OPS may remove the Chairperson from office for serious misconduct, incapacity, or failure to discharge the duties of the office, following consultation with the Committee. The Chairperson may resign at any time by written notice to the OPS. A vacancy in the office of Chairperson shall be filled as soon as practicable in accordance with clause 11.1.

---

**SECTION 12. MEMBERSHIP**

**12.1 Composition**

The Committee shall consist of no fewer than eight and no more than twelve members, appointed by the OPS. Members are drawn from:

- consumer advocacy organisations;
- industry and manufacturing associations;
- the retail sector;
- technical and scientific experts in product safety;
- legal experts with relevant experience; and
- representatives of relevant government agencies.

The OPS shall aim to ensure that the membership, taken as a whole, possesses an appropriate balance of skills, knowledge, and experience.

**12.2 Appointment and Term**

Members are appointed by the OPS for a term of three years, with effect from the date specified in their instrument of appointment. A member may be reappointed for a further term or terms. The OPS may, in its discretion, terminate a member's appointment at any time, after consultation with the Chairperson.
**13.1 Establishment**

The OPS shall provide secretariat services to the Committee. The secretariat shall be headed by a Secretariat Lead, who shall be an officer of the OPS or a person engaged by the OPS for that purpose. The Secretariat Lead is responsible for the day-to-day administration of the Committee and for ensuring that the Committee’s business is conducted in accordance with these Terms of Reference.

**13.2 Functions of the Secretariat**

The Secretariat shall:

- arrange meetings of the Committee, including the preparation and circulation of agendas, papers, and other documents required for meetings;
- attend all meetings of the Committee and record minutes of proceedings;
- maintain the Committee’s records, including minutes, papers, correspondence, and registers of members’ interests;
- manage the Committee’s correspondence and respond, on behalf of the Committee, to routine enquiries, subject to any directions of the Chairperson;
- coordinate the preparation of reports and other documents for approval by the Committee;
- maintain a register of decisions and action items arising from meetings, and track their implementation;
- provide administrative support to the Chairperson, the Deputy Chairperson, and members in the discharge of their functions;
- manage the Committee’s budget and expenditure, in accordance with OPS financial policies;
- arrange for the publication of the Committee’s reports, communiqués, and other public documents; and
- undertake such other functions as the Committee or the Chairperson may direct.

**13.3 Secretariat Lead**

The secretariat_lead of the Australian Consumer Product Safety Committee is Mr. David Okafor, as indicated in the committee's terms of reference. Record status: current. Mr. Okafor is the current Secretariat Lead and holds that office at the pleasure of the OPS. The Secretariat Lead shall:

- supervise the staff of the Secretariat and allocate duties among them;
- ensure that agendas and papers for each meeting are circulated no later than seven (7) clear days before the date of the meeting, unless the Chairperson directs otherwise;
- ensure that minutes of each meeting are prepared and circulated to members within fifteen (15) working days after the meeting, and that the minutes are confirmed, amended, or rejected at the next meeting;
- bring to the attention of the Chairperson, as soon as practicable, any matter that may require the Committee’s urgent consideration;
- act as the custodian of the Committee’s records and ensure their security and confidentiality;
- advise the Committee on procedural matters, including the application of these Terms of Reference;
- implement the Committee’s decisions and action items, or arrange for their implementation;
- report to the Committee, at least annually, on the operation of the Secretariat and on the implementation of decisions; and
- perform such other duties as the Committee or the Chairperson may direct.

The Secretariat Lead may delegate any of their functions to a member of the secretariat staff, provided that the delegation is recorded in writing and does not include the power to certify the minutes of a meeting.

**13.4 Staffing and Resources**

The OPS shall provide the Secretariat with adequate staff and resources to enable it to perform its functions. The Secretariat shall have access to legal, technical, and scientific advice as required, in accordance with arrangements approved by the OPS. The Secretariat may, with the approval of the Committee, engage consultants or contractors to assist with specific projects.

**13.5 Records and Confidentiality**

The records of the Committee are the property of the OPS. The Secretariat shall maintain the records in a manner that permits their retrieval and review. Records that are exempt from disclosure under the *Government Information (Public Access) Act 2009* (NSW) or any other applicable law shall be kept separately and marked accordingly. Members and the Secretariat shall treat as confidential all information received in the course of the Committee’s business that is not already in the public domain, except where disclosure is required by law or authorised by the Committee.
**14. Meeting Schedule**

**14.1 Regular Meetings**

The Committee shall meet quarterly in each calendar year. Meetings are ordinarily held in February, May, August, and November, unless the Chairperson, in consultation with the Secretariat, determines otherwise. The meeting_frequency of the Australian Consumer Product Safety Committee is quarterly, as stated in the committee's terms of reference. Record status: current.

The Secretariat shall circulate a schedule of proposed meeting dates for the following calendar year to all members no later than 30 November of the preceding year. The schedule shall be confirmed at the first meeting of the calendar year and may be varied only by decision of the Committee or by the Chairperson in exceptional circumstances.

Quarterly meetings shall be held in person unless the Chairperson determines that a meeting, or part of a meeting, be conducted by electronic or other means permitted by clause 15.3. Where a meeting is held in person, the venue shall be determined by the Secretariat in consultation with the Chairperson and communicated to members at least twenty-one (21) days before the meeting.

**14.2 Special Meetings**

A special meeting of the Committee may be convened at any time:

- by the Chairperson on the Chairperson’s own initiative;
- at the written request of the Minister; or
- at the written request of at least three (3) members of the Committee.

A request made by members under this clause shall state the business proposed to be transacted at the special meeting. No other business shall be transacted at a special meeting unless all members present agree.

Notice of a special meeting shall be given to members at least seven (7) days before the meeting, unless the Chairperson determines that a shorter notice period is necessary due to the urgency of the matter. The notice shall state the date, time, venue, and the business to be considered.

**14.3 Electronic Meetings**

Meetings may be conducted using electronic communication where the Chairperson is satisfied that the technology used enables all participants to hear and be heard by each other simultaneously, and that the integrity of the meeting is otherwise maintained. A member participating by electronic means is taken to be present at the meeting.

**14.4 Meeting Dates and Venue – Logistical Provisions**

The Secretariat shall, in consultation with the Chairperson, ensure that meeting venues are accessible to members, including those with disability. Meeting papers shall be distributed electronically unless a member requests a hard copy. Papers shall be distributed no later than five (5) working days before the meeting, except where the Chairperson authorises a shorter period.

The Secretariat shall maintain a register of proposed meeting dates and venues, and shall update it promptly when changes are made. The register shall be available to members on request.

**14.5 Cancellation or Postponement**

The Chairperson may cancel or postpone a scheduled quarterly meeting where, in the Chairperson’s opinion, there is insufficient business to justify holding the meeting, or where unforeseen circumstances make it impracticable to proceed. Where a meeting is cancelled or postponed, the Secretariat shall notify members as soon as practicable and shall propose an alternative date.

**15. Conduct of Meetings**

**15.1 Quorum** – *Note: this clause is reserved for the Committee’s consideration of quorum arrangements and is not in effect.*

**15.2 Chairperson**

The Chairperson shall preside at all meetings of the Committee at which the Chairperson is present. In the absence of the Chairperson, the Deputy Chairperson shall preside. In the absence of both the Chairperson and the Deputy Chairperson, the members present shall elect one of their number to preside at that meeting.

**15.3 Participation by Electronic Means**

A member who is unable to attend a meeting in person may participate by telephone, video conference, or other electronic means, provided that the member can hear and be heard by all other participants. A member participating by electronic means shall be counted as present for the purposes of the meeting.
**15.1 Quorum**

The quorum_requirement of the Australian Consumer Product Safety Committee is majority of members, as defined in the committee's terms of reference. Record status: current. No item of business shall be transacted at a meeting of the Committee unless a quorum is present. For the avoidance of doubt, a quorum shall be constituted by a majority of the members currently holding office, whether they are present in person or participating by electronic means in accordance with clause 15.3. A member who has declared a conflict of interest and has withdrawn from the meeting in accordance with clause 16 shall not be counted towards the quorum for the duration of that withdrawal. Should a quorum cease to be present during the course of a meeting, the Chairperson shall suspend the meeting until such time as a quorum is again present, or shall adjourn the meeting to a later date.

**15.2 Chairperson** *(as previously recorded)*

The Chairperson shall preside at all meetings of the Committee at which the Chairperson is present. In the absence of the Chairperson, the Deputy Chairperson shall preside. In the absence of both the Chairperson and the Deputy Chairperson, the members present shall elect one of their number to preside at that meeting.

**15.3 Participation by Electronic Means** *(as previously recorded)*

A member who is unable to attend a meeting in person may participate by telephone, video conference, or other electronic means, provided that the member can hear and be heard by all other participants. A member participating by electronic means shall be counted as present for the purposes of the meeting.

**16. Conflict of Interest**

**16.1 Declaration**

A member who has a material personal interest in a matter before the Committee must declare that interest to the Chairperson as soon as practicable after becoming aware of the matter, and in any event before the matter is discussed. The declaration shall be recorded in the minutes of the meeting.

**16.2 Withdrawal**

Following a declaration under clause 16.1, the member concerned shall withdraw from the meeting while the matter is discussed and shall not participate in any vote on the matter, unless the Chairperson determines otherwise with the agreement of the other members present. A member who has withdrawn shall not be counted towards the quorum for the purposes of that item.

**16.3 Standing Declarations**

A member may make a standing declaration of interest in a class of matters. A standing declaration shall be recorded in the minutes and shall have effect for the period specified in the declaration.

**17. Voting**

**17.1 General**

Except where otherwise provided in this Charter, a question arising at a meeting of the Committee shall be decided by a majority of the votes of the members present and voting on the question. Each member present has one vote on each question. The Chairperson has a deliberative vote only, and does not have a casting vote. In the event of an equality of votes, the question shall be taken to have been negatived.

**17.2 Abstentions**

A member who abstains from voting on a question shall be recorded as having abstained. An abstention shall not be counted as a vote for or against the question. A member who has withdrawn from the meeting under clause 16.2 shall not be recorded as having abstained on the question.

**17.3 Voting by Show of Hands**

Voting shall ordinarily be conducted by a show of hands, unless the Chairperson determines, or a member requests, that a ballot be conducted. The result of a ballot shall be recorded in the minutes.

**17.4 Rescission of Decisions**

A decision of the Committee may be rescinded or varied at a subsequent meeting by a resolution passed by a majority of the members present and voting, provided that notice of the proposed rescission or variation has been included in the agenda for that meeting.

**18. Decision-Making Procedures**

**18.1 Consensus Seeking**

The Committee shall, where practicable, seek to make decisions by consensus. Where consensus is not achieved, the matter shall be determined by a vote in accordance with clause 17.
**18.2 Motions and Amendments**

A motion before the Committee shall be proposed and seconded. An amendment to a motion may be moved and shall be debated and voted upon before the motion as amended, or the motion as originally proposed, is put to the vote. A motion that has been moved and seconded may be withdrawn by the mover with the consent of the Committee.

**18.3 Minutes of Meetings**

Minutes of each meeting shall be recorded and shall include the names of members present, the names of members absent, and the decisions taken. Draft minutes shall be circulated to members within fifteen (15) business days of the meeting and shall be confirmed at the next meeting of the Committee. Confirmed minutes shall be made available on the Office of Product Safety website, subject to any redactions made in accordance with clause 16.1.

**19. Membership**

**19.1 Categories of Membership**

The Committee shall consist of no more than twelve (12) members, appointed by the Minister for Consumer Affairs (the Minister) in accordance with this clause. Membership shall comprise the following categories:

(a) a Chairperson;

(b) one (1) member with expertise in consumer product safety policy, drawn from an Australian Government agency;

(c) one (1) member with expertise in product safety regulation, drawn from a State or Territory government agency;

(d) two (2) members representing consumer interests, nominated by consumer organisations;

(e) two (2) members representing the manufacturing and retail industries, nominated by industry associations;

(f) one (1) member with expertise in product design, engineering, or quality assurance, nominated by a professional body;

(g) one (1) member with expertise in legal practice relating to product liability or consumer protection;

(h) one (1) member with expertise in standards development, nominated by a standards organisation; and

(i) two (2) members with expertise in other relevant fields, such as public health, injury prevention, or data analysis, appointed at the discretion of the Minister.

**19.2 Appointment Process**

The Minister shall appoint members by written instrument. Before making an appointment, the Minister shall:

(a) advertise the vacancy publicly, including on the Office of Product Safety website, unless the Minister is satisfied that the vacancy should be filled without public advertisement; and

(b) consider nominations received from the bodies referred to in clause 19.1, as well as expressions of interest from the public.

**19.3 Terms of Appointment**

A member shall be appointed for a term of up to three (3) years, as specified in the instrument of appointment. A member may be reappointed for one further term of up to three (3) years, provided that no member shall serve for more than six (6) consecutive years. A member appointed to fill a casual vacancy shall be appointed for the remainder of the term of the member being replaced.

**19.4 Remuneration and Expenses**

Members other than the Chairperson shall be remunerated at the rate determined by the Remuneration Tribunal. The Chairperson shall be remunerated at the rate determined by the Remuneration Tribunal for the Chairperson of a statutory committee. Members shall be reimbursed for reasonable expenses incurred in connection with their duties, including travel and accommodation, in accordance with Office of Product Safety policies.

**19.5 Cessation of Membership**

The office of a member becomes vacant if the member:

(a) dies;

(b) resigns by written notice to the Minister;

(c) is removed from office by the Minister under clause 19.6;

(d) is absent, without the approval of the Chairperson, from three (3) consecutive meetings of the Committee; or

(e) becomes bankrupt, applies to take the benefit of any law for the relief of bankrupt or insolvent debtors, or compounds with his or her creditors.

**19.6 Removal from Office**

The Minister may remove a member from office for misbehaviour, incapacity, or failure to comply with the obligations set out in this Charter, including the obligations in clause 15 (Confidentiality) and clause 16 (Conflicts of Interest). Before removing a member, the Minister shall give the member written notice of the proposed removal and an opportunity to make submissions within a reasonable period specified in the notice.
**20. Subcommittees and Working Groups**

**20.1 Establishment**

The Committee may, from time to time, establish subcommittees and working groups to assist it in carrying out its functions. A subcommittee or working group may be established:

(a) on the initiative of the Committee;

(b) at the request of the Minister; or

(c) at the request of the Office of Product Safety (OPS), where the matter falls within the Committee's functions.

**20.2 Purpose**

Subcommittees and working groups shall be established for a specific purpose, which shall be set out in the instrument establishing the body. The purpose may include:

(a) examining a particular product safety issue or class of products;

(b) developing draft advice or recommendations for consideration by the Committee;

(c) reviewing technical standards, testing protocols, or research findings;

(d) consulting with stakeholders, including industry bodies, consumer groups, and relevant government agencies; or

(e) undertaking any other task that the Committee considers appropriate.

**20.3 Terms of Reference**

Each subcommittee and working group shall have written terms of reference, approved by the Committee, which shall include:

(a) the name of the body;

(b) its purpose and scope of work;

(c) its membership, including the Chairperson of the body;

(d) reporting requirements, including the timing and format of reports to the Committee;

(e) the expected duration of the body, including any milestones or review points;

(f) resource requirements and any budget implications; and

(g) any specific limitations on the body's authority.

Terms of reference shall be reviewed by the Committee at least annually or when there is a significant change in the body's scope or membership.

**20.4 Membership of Subcommittees and Working Groups**

Unless the Committee determines otherwise, a subcommittee or working group shall consist of:

(a) at least one (1) member of the Committee, who shall be appointed as Chairperson of the body; and

(b) such other persons as the Committee appoints, who may include:

(i) other members of the Committee;

(ii) officers of OPS;

(iii) representatives of other government agencies;

(iv) representatives of industry, consumer organisations, or professional bodies; and

(v) individuals with relevant expertise, including academics, scientists, engineers, or legal practitioners.

Persons appointed under paragraph (b) need not be members of the Committee. Appointments shall be made by the Committee on the recommendation of the Chairperson, unless the Committee determines otherwise in a particular case.

**20.5 Procedure**

The procedure of a subcommittee or working group shall be as determined by the body, provided that:

(a) the body shall meet as often as necessary to complete its work;

(b) the Chairperson of the body shall preside at its meetings;

(c) decisions of the body shall be made by consensus wherever possible, and otherwise by a majority of the members present and voting;

(d) a record of the body's proceedings and decisions shall be kept and provided to the Committee; and

(e) the body may invite persons to attend its meetings for particular items, with the agreement of the Chairperson of the body.

**20.6 Reporting**

A subcommittee or working group shall report to the Committee:

(a) at each ordinary meeting of the Committee, unless the terms of reference provide otherwise; and

(b) at any other time as the Committee or the Chairperson of the Committee may require.

A report shall include a summary of the body's activities since its last report, any findings or recommendations, and any matters requiring a decision by the Committee.

**20.7 Dissolution**

A subcommittee or working group shall be dissolved:

(a) when it has completed its task, as certified by the Committee;

(b) on the expiry of any period specified in its terms of reference; or

(c) at any time by resolution of the Committee.

On dissolution, any records of the body shall be transferred to the Secretary of the Committee, unless the Committee directs otherwise.
**21. Reporting and Accountability**

**21.1 Reporting to the Office of Product Safety**

The Committee shall report to the Office of Product Safety (OPS) on the exercise of its functions and powers under this Charter.

(a) The Chairperson shall provide to the Secretary of OPS, or to such other officer as OPS may direct, a written report of each ordinary meeting of the Committee, no later than ten (10) business days after the meeting.

(b) The report shall include:

(i) a list of members present and apologies tendered;

(ii) a summary of matters considered, including any recommendations made or decisions taken;

(iii) any advice provided to OPS on proposed recalls, safety warning notices, or other regulatory action;

(iv) any matters on which the Committee was unable to reach consensus, and the nature of the disagreement; and

(v) any other matter the Committee considers should be brought to the attention of OPS.

(c) In addition to the reports under paragraph (a), the Committee shall provide to OPS:

(i) a written report on any urgent matter as soon as practicable after the matter has been considered, and in any event no later than five (5) business days after consideration; and

(ii) such other reports or information as OPS may reasonably request in writing.

(d) Reports provided under this clause shall be prepared by the Secretary in consultation with the Chairperson. The Secretary shall ensure that reports are accurate, complete, and reflect the views of the Committee as a whole, except where a dissenting view is recorded under paragraph (b)(iv).

**21.2 Annual Report**

(a) The Committee shall prepare an annual report on its activities for each financial year, covering the period from 1 July to 30 June.

(b) The annual report shall be provided to OPS no later than 31 August following the end of the financial year to which it relates.

(c) The annual report shall include:

(i) a statement of the Committee's membership during the year, including appointments, resignations, and the dates of such changes;

(ii) the number of meetings held, and the attendance record of each member;

(iii) a summary of the matters considered by the Committee during the year, including the number of product safety investigations reviewed and the number of recall recommendations made;

(iv) a summary of the work of any subcommittees or working groups established under clause 20, including their terms of reference and outcomes;

(v) a statement of any conflicts of interest declared and how they were managed;

(vi) a review of the Committee's performance against its functions and any relevant performance indicators; and

(vii) any recommendations for amendments to this Charter or for improvements to the product safety framework.

(d) The annual report shall be made publicly available on the OPS website, subject to the confidentiality provisions in clause 22.

**21.3 Public Transparency**

(a) The Committee is committed to transparency in its operations, subject to the need to protect confidential commercial information and personal privacy.

(b) The following documents shall be published on the OPS website as soon as practicable after they are finalised:

(i) this Charter and any amendments to it;

(ii) the Committee's annual reports;

(iii) a summary of each recall recommendation made by the Committee, including the product concerned and the reason for the recommendation;

(iv) a list of current members and their terms of appointment; and

(v) such other documents as OPS may determine.

(c) Documents published under paragraph (b) shall be published in a format that is accessible to members of the public, including persons with disability.

(d) The Committee shall not publish, and OPS shall not publish on the Committee's behalf, any information that is:

(i) confidential commercial information, including trade secrets or manufacturing processes;

(ii) personal information within the meaning of the Privacy Act 1988 (Cth), except as required by law; or

This Charter is current as at the date of the latest version above. Superseded versions are retained on the OPS website for historical reference only and do not reflect the current operating arrangements of the Committee.

---

**PART A – ESTABLISHMENT AND FUNCTION**

**1. Establishment**

The Product Safety Committee (the Committee) is established under section 18 of the *Product Safety Act 2011* (Cth) as an advisory committee to the Office of Product Safety (OPS).

**2. Mission**

The Committee provides expert advice to the Minister and the OPS on matters relating to the safety of consumer products, including the identification of emerging risks, the evaluation of product safety data, and the prioritisation of regulatory action.

**3. Functions**

The functions of the Committee are:

(a) to advise on the safety of consumer products and on priorities for product safety action;

(b) to review and make recommendations on proposed recall actions;

(c) to advise on the development and review of product safety standards;

(d) to identify emerging product safety issues and recommend research or investigation; and

(e) to perform such other functions as the Minister or OPS may refer to the Committee.

**4. Powers**

The Committee may:

(a) obtain information from any Commonwealth, State or Territory agency;

(b) consult with industry, consumer groups, and technical experts;

(c) establish subcommittees or working groups in accordance with clause 20; and

(d) conduct such inquiries as are reasonably necessary to perform its functions.

**5. Independence**

The Committee performs its functions independently and is not subject to direction by the Minister or OPS in relation to the content of its advice. However, the Committee's advice is advisory only and does not bind the Minister or OPS.

---

**PART B – MEMBERSHIP**

**6. Composition**

(a) The Committee consists of no fewer than seven and no more than eleven members.

(b) The Minister appoints members for a term not exceeding three years. A member may be reappointed.

(c) In appointing members, the Minister must have regard to:

(i) the need for expertise in product safety, consumer affairs, engineering, toxicology, epidemiology, and law; and

(ii) the need for a balance of perspectives, including industry, consumer, and academic perspectives.

(d) The Minister must appoint one member as Chair. The Chair holds office for a term not exceeding three years and may be reappointed.

(e) The Minister may appoint a Deputy Chair from among the members. The Deputy Chair acts as Chair in the absence of the Chair.

**7. Appointment process**

(a) Vacancies are advertised on the OPS website and through relevant professional networks.

(b) The Minister may also appoint a member without advertisement where the Minister considers that a particular expertise is required.

(c) Appointments are made by written instrument signed by the Minister.

**8. Remuneration**

Members are entitled to remuneration and allowances as determined by the Remuneration Tribunal. Members who are employed by the Commonwealth are not entitled to additional remuneration for their service on the Committee.

**9. Disclosure of interests**

(a) Each member must, on appointment and at the start of each meeting, disclose any interest that could conflict with the proper performance of the Committee's functions.
**PART C – OPERATIONS AND PROCEDURES** *(continued)*

**10. Meetings**

(a) The Committee must meet at least four times in each calendar year.

(b) The Chair may convene additional meetings where the Chair considers it necessary. The Chair must convene a meeting within 14 days of receiving a written request from at least three members.

(c) Meetings may be held in person, by telephone, by video conference, or by a combination of these means. A member who participates by telephone or video conference is taken to be present at the meeting.

(d) The Chair presides at all meetings at which the Chair is present. In the absence of the Chair, the Deputy Chair presides. If both the Chair and Deputy Chair are absent, the members present must elect one of their number to preside.

(e) The Committee may invite other persons to attend a meeting or part of a meeting for the purpose of advising the Committee. An invited person has no right to vote.

(f) Subject to this Charter, the Committee may regulate its own proceedings.

**11. Quorum**

(a) The quorum for a meeting is one-half of the members holding office at the time of the meeting, rounded up to the nearest whole number, provided that at least four members are present.

(b) A decision of the Committee is not valid unless made at a meeting at which a quorum is present.

(c) If a meeting is adjourned for want of a quorum, the Chair must reconvene the meeting within 21 days. Notice of the reconvened meeting must be given to all members at least 7 days before the reconvened meeting.

**12. Voting**

(a) Decisions of the Committee are made by a majority of the votes cast by members present and voting.

(b) Each member present has one vote. The person presiding has a deliberative vote and, in the event of an equality of votes, also has a casting vote.

(c) A member who has a material personal interest in a matter before the Committee must not vote on that matter. The member must also absent themselves from the room while the matter is discussed, unless the Committee resolves otherwise.

(d) The Committee may decide a matter by a written resolution signed by all members entitled to vote on the matter. A written resolution is as valid as a resolution passed at a meeting.

**13. Minutes and records**

(a) The Committee must keep accurate minutes of each meeting. The minutes must record:

(i) the names of the members present and any apologies; and

(ii) the decisions made and the reasons for those decisions, including any dissenting views.

(b) Minutes of a meeting are to be confirmed at the next meeting and signed by the person presiding at that next meeting.

(c) The Committee must make available, on the OPS website, a summary of each meeting's outcomes within 10 business days after the meeting. The summary must not disclose information that is confidential or commercially sensitive.

(d) The Committee must keep a register of members' interests. The register is to be made available for inspection on request, subject to the Privacy Act 1988 (Cth).

**14. Subcommittees and working groups**

(a) The Committee may establish subcommittees and working groups to assist it in performing its functions.

(b) A subcommittee or working group must report to the Committee at each meeting of the Committee.

(c) A subcommittee or working group may include persons who are not members of the Committee. Such persons have no right to vote.

(d) The Committee must review the need for each subcommittee and working group at least once each year.

**PART D – DISSOLUTION AND FINAL PROVISIONS**

**15. Dissolution**

(a) The Committee continues in existence until dissolved by the Minister by written instrument published on the OPS website and in the Commonwealth of Australia Gazette.

(b) Before dissolving the Committee, the Minister must:

(i) consult the Chair of the Committee; and

(ii) give the Committee at least 90 days' notice in writing of the proposed dissolution.

(c) On dissolution, the Committee must, within 60 days, provide to the Minister a final report on its activities. The final report must include a summary of any outstanding matters and recommendations that the Committee considers should be brought to the Minister's attention.

2015/01 – Household Cots and Folding Cots Safety Standard
Adopted: 12/03/2015
Effective: 01/06/2015
Source instrument: Consumer Goods Safety Standard (Household Cots and Folding Cots) Instrument 2015
Summary: Prescribes requirements for the structural integrity, drop-side mechanisms, and mattress
base support of household cots and folding cots. Includes labelling requirements for warnings and
assembly instructions.
Notes: Reviewed 2018 – no amendment required. Reviewed again 2021 – no amendment required.

2015/02 – Baby Walkers Safety Standard
Adopted: 12/03/2015
Effective: 01/06/2015
Source instrument: Consumer Goods Safety Standard (Baby Walkers) Instrument 2015
Summary: Sets performance requirements to prevent stair falls and tip-overs. Includes testing
requirements for dynamic stability and wheel resistance.
Notes: Industry consultation in 2019 raised the question of whether the standard should be expanded
to cover activity centres. No change made at that time. Under review again as of Q3 2023.

2016/01 – Pedal Bicycle Safety Standard
Adopted: 08/09/2016
Effective: 01/12/2016
Source instrument: Consumer Goods Safety Standard (Pedal Bicycles) Instrument 2016
Summary: Applies to bicycles for children (wheel diameter 16–24 inches) and adults (wheel diameter
26 inches or more). Covers braking, steering, and reflector requirements.
Notes: Amendment 2019/03 added requirements for reflectors to be visible from the front, rear, and
sides. No other amendments.

2017/01 – Consumer Goods Safety Standard 2017
Adopted: 01/06/2017
Effective: 01/09/2017
Source instrument: Consumer Goods Safety Standard 2017 (Instrument No. 2017/01)
Summary: Consolidates and replaces the previous separate standards for a range of consumer goods,
including:
- Baby walkers (previously 2015/02)
- Household cots and folding cots (previously 2015/01)
- Children's nightwear and paper patterns (previously 2015/04)
- Cosmetic products containing certain restricted substances
- Toaster ovens and similar appliances
The standard sets out general safety requirements, testing protocols, and labelling obligations.
It also introduces a new requirement for suppliers to retain technical documentation for five (5)
years from the date of supply.
Notes: Consumer Goods Safety Standard 2017 adoption_date 2017-06-01. Record status: current. This standard is the primary
consolidating instrument for the listed product categories. The previous separate standards remain
in force in parallel for a transition period of six (6) months from the effective date, after which
they are superseded. See archived section for the transition arrangement.
Amendments:
- 2018/01 – Clarification of testing protocol for toaster ovens (effective 01/03/2018)
- 2020/02 – Update to labelling requirements for cosmetic products (effective 01/08/2020)
No further amendments to date.

2018/02 – Portable Swimming Pool Fences Safety Standard
Adopted: 14/05/2018
Effective: 01/08/2018
Source instrument: Consumer Goods Safety Standard (Portable Swimming Pool Fences) Instrument 2018
Summary: Specifies performance requirements for portable fencing intended to restrict access to
swimming pools. Includes requirements for gate latches, panel strength, and self-closing mechanisms.
Notes: This standard was developed following a rise in incidents involving portable pool fences.
It does not apply to fixed in-ground fencing, which is covered by building regulations.

2019/01 – Cordless Window Blinds Safety Standard
Adopted: 22/02/2019
Effective: 01/06/2019
Source instrument: Consumer Goods Safety Standard (Cordless Window Blinds) Instrument 2019
Summary: Requires that all window blinds and window coverings supplied in Australia must be cordless
or have inaccessible cords. Applies to blinds with a continuous loop cord, inner cord, or any cord
that could form a loop.
Notes: This standard was introduced in response to the risk of strangulation for young children.
It applies to both custom-made and ready-made blinds. The standard also covers existing blinds when
they are re-supplied or re-fitted.
2019/02 – Button Battery Safety Standard
Adopted: 10/04/2019
Effective: 01/07/2019
Source instrument: Consumer Goods Safety Standard (Button Batteries) Instrument 2019
Summary: Sets mandatory requirements for the secure compartment of button battery
compartments in consumer goods, and for the supply of button batteries themselves.
Applies to all products that contain or may contain button batteries, including
remote controls, watches, toys, and novelty items.
Notes: Developed following a coronial inquest into the death of a young child. The
standard requires that compartments be resistant to opening by children under five
years, and that batteries be supplied in child-resistant packaging. Products that
are exempt include hearing aids and other medical devices where the battery
compartment is essential to function and cannot be made secure without affecting
operation. Suppliers must also include a warning label on packaging and in the
product instructions. The standard does not require retrofitting of products
already supplied before the effective date.
Amendments:
- 2020/03 – Clarification of test method for compartment torque and pull forces
  (effective 01/11/2020)
- 2021/04 – Extension of scope to include lithium coin cell batteries with a
  diameter of 16 mm or greater (effective 01/03/2022)

2019/03 – Baby Walkers Safety Standard
Adopted: 12/06/2019
Effective: 01/09/2019
Source instrument: Consumer Goods Safety Standard (Baby Walkers) Instrument 2019
Summary: Prohibits the supply of baby walkers that are not fitted with a braking
mechanism capable of stopping the walker at the edge of a step or stairway.
Notes: This standard revives and updates the previous 2013 standard which had
lapsed. The braking mechanism must be tested in accordance with the test method
set out in AS/NZS 8124.1. The standard does not apply to walkers that are
designed to be stationary (i.e. without wheels). Suppliers must retain test
reports for a period of five (5) years.

2020/01 – High-Powered Magnet Set Safety Standard
Adopted: 20/02/2020
Effective: 01/05/2020
Source instrument: Consumer Goods Safety Standard (High-Powered Magnet Sets) Instrument 2020
Summary: Requires that high-powered magnet sets (sets of separable magnets with a
magnetic flux index of 50 kG² mm² or greater) be supplied only in packaging that
is child-resistant and carry a warning label stating that the product is not
suitable for children under 14 years of age.
Notes: The standard was introduced in response to a series of serious intestinal
injuries in older children and teenagers resulting from the ingestion of multiple
magnets. In addition to packaging and labelling requirements, the standard
prohibits the supply of high-powered magnet sets in a form that is not enclosed
in a child-resistant container. The standard does not apply to magnets that are
sold as part of an educational or scientific kit where the magnets are not
intended to be separated from the kit. This standard is the first to rely on the
magnetic flux index as a threshold criterion. Suppliers should note that the test
method for flux index is specified in the instrument and differs from the method
used in the 2015 voluntary code.

2020/02 – Baby Bath Aids Safety Standard
Adopted: 18/06/2020
Effective: 01/09/2020
Source instrument: Consumer Goods Safety Standard (Baby Bath Aids) Instrument 2020
Summary: Prohibits the supply of baby bath aids (including bath seats, bath rings,
and bath cradles) that are not fitted with a warning label instructing the user
to never leave a child unattended in the bath.
Notes: This standard was adopted following a review of incidents where bath aids
gave caregivers a false sense of security. The warning label must be permanently
affixed to the product and be visible when the product is in use. The standard
does not apply to bath aids that are intended for use by children over two years
of age, or to products that are designed to be held by a caregiver (e.g. a bath
sling). No amendments to date.

Members are appointed for a term of three years, with the possibility of reappointment. The OPS may appoint additional members on a temporary or project-specific basis where specialist expertise is required.

The current membership roster is maintained by the OPS Secretariat and is published on the OPS website. Any changes to membership are recorded in the minutes of the next Committee meeting.

**4. MEETING FREQUENCY AND CONVENING**

The Committee shall meet at least four times per calendar year. Additional meetings may be convened at the request of the OPS or the Committee Chair.

Meetings may be held in person, by teleconference, or by videoconference. A quorum shall consist of a majority of appointed members. Decisions of the Committee shall generally be made by consensus; where consensus cannot be reached, decisions shall be made by a simple majority of members present and voting. The Chair has a deliberative vote only.

**5. OPERATING PRINCIPLES**

In conducting its business, the Committee shall:

(a) act in good faith and in the public interest;
(b) base its advice on the best available evidence, including scientific research, incident data, and stakeholder input;
(c) declare and manage any conflicts of interest in accordance with the procedures set out in Section 7;
(d) maintain the confidentiality of commercially sensitive information and any other information marked as confidential by the OPS;
(e) support the OPS in meeting its statutory obligations under the *Competition and Consumer Act 2010* (Cth) and associated regulations.

**6. SUBCOMMITTEES AND WORKING GROUPS**

The Committee may establish subcommittees or working groups to examine specific issues in detail. Such bodies must report to the full Committee and do not have decision-making authority. The terms of reference for any subcommittee or working group shall be agreed by the Committee and recorded in the minutes.

Australian Consumer Product Safety Committee established_date 2015-03-12. Record status: current.

**7. CONFLICT OF INTEREST**

Members are required to disclose any actual, potential, or perceived conflict of interest at the commencement of each meeting agenda item where such a conflict arises. The disclosure shall be recorded in the minutes. A member with a material conflict shall withdraw from the discussion and any decision-making on the relevant item, unless otherwise determined by the Committee.

**8. SECRETARIAT AND SUPPORT**

The OPS provides secretariat support to the Committee, including the preparation of agendas, circulation of papers, and recording of minutes. The Secretariat is responsible for maintaining the Committee's records and for facilitating communication between members and the OPS.

**9. REPORTING AND ACCOUNTABILITY**

The Committee shall report to the OPS after each meeting, providing a summary of its deliberations and any recommendations. The OPS may request the Committee to provide a more detailed report on specific matters. The Committee's annual report shall be published on the OPS website.

**10. REVIEW OF THIS CHARTER**

This Charter shall be reviewed every three years, or earlier if significant changes to the Committee's role or operating environment warrant such a review. Amendments to this Charter are made by the OPS in consultation with the Committee.

**14. Meeting Schedule**

**14.1 Regular Meetings**

The Committee shall meet quarterly in each calendar year. Meetings are ordinarily held in February, May, August, and November, unless the Chairperson, in consultation with the Secretariat, determines otherwise. The meeting_frequency of the Australian Consumer Product Safety Committee is quarterly, as stated in the committee's terms of reference. Record status: current.

The Secretariat shall circulate a schedule of proposed meeting dates for the following calendar year to all members no later than 30 November of the preceding year. The schedule shall be confirmed at the first meeting of the calendar year and may be varied only by decision of the Committee or by the Chairperson in exceptional circumstances.

Quarterly meetings shall be held in person unless the Chairperson determines that a meeting, or part of a meeting, be conducted by electronic or other means permitted by clause 15.3. Where a meeting is held in person, the venue shall be determined by the Secretariat in consultation with the Chairperson and communicated to members at least twenty-one (21) days before the meeting.

**14.2 Special Meetings**

A special meeting of the Committee may be convened at any time:

- by the Chairperson on the Chairperson’s own initiative;
- at the written request of the Minister; or
- at the written request of at least three (3) members of the Committee.

A request made by members under this clause shall state the business proposed to be transacted at the special meeting. No other business shall be transacted at a special meeting unless all members present agree.

Notice of a special meeting shall be given to members at least seven (7) days before the meeting, unless the Chairperson determines that a shorter notice period is necessary due to the urgency of the matter. The notice shall state the date, time, venue, and the business to be considered.

**14.3 Electronic Meetings**

Meetings may be conducted using electronic communication where the Chairperson is satisfied that the technology used enables all participants to hear and be heard by each other simultaneously, and that the integrity of the meeting is otherwise maintained. A member participating by electronic means is taken to be present at the meeting.

**14.4 Meeting Dates and Venue – Logistical Provisions**

The Secretariat shall, in consultation with the Chairperson, ensure that meeting venues are accessible to members, including those with disability. Meeting papers shall be distributed electronically unless a member requests a hard copy. Papers shall be distributed no later than five (5) working days before the meeting, except where the Chairperson authorises a shorter period.

The Secretariat shall maintain a register of proposed meeting dates and venues, and shall update it promptly when changes are made. The register shall be available to members on request.

**14.5 Cancellation or Postponement**

The Chairperson may cancel or postpone a scheduled quarterly meeting where, in the Chairperson’s opinion, there is insufficient business to justify holding the meeting, or where unforeseen circumstances make it impracticable to proceed. Where a meeting is cancelled or postponed, the Secretariat shall notify members as soon as practicable and shall propose an alternative date.

**15. Conduct of Meetings**

**15.1 Quorum** – *Note: this clause is reserved for the Committee’s consideration of quorum arrangements and is not in effect.*

**15.2 Chairperson**

The Chairperson shall preside at all meetings of the Committee at which the Chairperson is present. In the absence of the Chairperson, the Deputy Chairperson shall preside. In the absence of both the Chairperson and the Deputy Chairperson, the members present shall elect one of their number to preside at that meeting.

**15.3 Participation by Electronic Means**

A member who is unable to attend a meeting in person may participate by telephone, video conference, or other electronic means, provided that the member can hear and be heard by all other participants. A member participating by electronic means shall be counted as present for the purposes of the meeting.

**15.1 Quorum**

The quorum_requirement of the Australian Consumer Product Safety Committee is majority of members, as defined in the committee's terms of reference. Record status: current. No item of business shall be transacted at a meeting of the Committee unless a quorum is present. For the avoidance of doubt, a quorum shall be constituted by a majority of the members currently holding office, whether they are present in person or participating by electronic means in accordance with clause 15.3. A member who has declared a conflict of interest and has withdrawn from the meeting in accordance with clause 16 shall not be counted towards the quorum for the duration of that withdrawal. Should a quorum cease to be present during the course of a meeting, the Chairperson shall suspend the meeting until such time as a quorum is again present, or shall adjourn the meeting to a later date.

**15.2 Chairperson** *(as previously recorded)*

The Chairperson shall preside at all meetings of the Committee at which the Chairperson is present. In the absence of the Chairperson, the Deputy Chairperson shall preside. In the absence of both the Chairperson and the Deputy Chairperson, the members present shall elect one of their number to preside at that meeting.

**15.3 Participation by Electronic Means** *(as previously recorded)*

A member who is unable to attend a meeting in person may participate by telephone, video conference, or other electronic means, provided that the member can hear and be heard by all other participants. A member participating by electronic means shall be counted as present for the purposes of the meeting.

**16. Conflict of Interest**

**16.1 Declaration**

A member who has a material personal interest in a matter before the Committee must declare that interest to the Chairperson as soon as practicable after becoming aware of the matter, and in any event before the matter is discussed. The declaration shall be recorded in the minutes of the meeting.

**16.2 Withdrawal**

Following a declaration under clause 16.1, the member concerned shall withdraw from the meeting while the matter is discussed and shall not participate in any vote on the matter, unless the Chairperson determines otherwise with the agreement of the other members present. A member who has withdrawn shall not be counted towards the quorum for the purposes of that item.

**16.3 Standing Declarations**

A member may make a standing declaration of interest in a class of matters. A standing declaration shall be recorded in the minutes and shall have effect for the period specified in the declaration.

**17. Voting**

**17.1 General**

Except where otherwise provided in this Charter, a question arising at a meeting of the Committee shall be decided by a majority of the votes of the members present and voting on the question. Each member present has one vote on each question. The Chairperson has a deliberative vote only, and does not have a casting vote. In the event of an equality of votes, the question shall be taken to have been negatived.

**17.2 Abstentions**

A member who abstains from voting on a question shall be recorded as having abstained. An abstention shall not be counted as a vote for or against the question. A member who has withdrawn from the meeting under clause 16.2 shall not be recorded as having abstained on the question.

**17.3 Voting by Show of Hands**

Voting shall ordinarily be conducted by a show of hands, unless the Chairperson determines, or a member requests, that a ballot be conducted. The result of a ballot shall be recorded in the minutes.

**17.4 Rescission of Decisions**

A decision of the Committee may be rescinded or varied at a subsequent meeting by a resolution passed by a majority of the members present and voting, provided that notice of the proposed rescission or variation has been included in the agenda for that meeting.

**18. Decision-Making Procedures**

**18.1 Consensus Seeking**

The Committee shall, where practicable, seek to make decisions by consensus. Where consensus is not achieved, the matter shall be determined by a vote in accordance with clause 17.

(a) The quorum for a meeting is one-half of the members holding office at the time of the meeting, rounded up to the nearest whole number, provided that at least four members are present.

(b) A decision of the Committee is not valid unless made at a meeting at which a quorum is present.

(c) If a meeting is adjourned for want of a quorum, the Chair must reconvene the meeting within 21 days. Notice of the reconvened meeting must be given to all members at least 7 days before the reconvened meeting.

**12. Voting**

(a) Decisions of the Committee are made by a majority of the votes cast by members present and voting.

(b) Each member present has one vote. The person presiding has a deliberative vote and, in the event of an equality of votes, also has a casting vote.

(c) A member who has a material personal interest in a matter before the Committee must not vote on that matter. The member must also absent themselves from the room while the matter is discussed, unless the Committee resolves otherwise.

(d) The Committee may decide a matter by a written resolution signed by all members entitled to vote on the matter. A written resolution is as valid as a resolution passed at a meeting.

**13. Minutes and records**

(a) The Committee must keep accurate minutes of each meeting. The minutes must record:

(i) the names of the members present and any apologies; and

(ii) the decisions made and the reasons for those decisions, including any dissenting views.

(b) Minutes of a meeting are to be confirmed at the next meeting and signed by the person presiding at that next meeting.

(c) The Committee must make available, on the OPS website, a summary of each meeting's outcomes within 10 business days after the meeting. The summary must not disclose information that is confidential or commercially sensitive.

(d) The Committee must keep a register of members' interests. The register is to be made available for inspection on request, subject to the Privacy Act 1988 (Cth).

**14. Subcommittees and working groups**

(a) The Committee may establish subcommittees and working groups to assist it in performing its functions.

(b) A subcommittee or working group must report to the Committee at each meeting of the Committee.

(c) A subcommittee or working group may include persons who are not members of the Committee. Such persons have no right to vote.

(d) The Committee must review the need for each subcommittee and working group at least once each year.

**PART D – DISSOLUTION AND FINAL PROVISIONS**

**15. Dissolution**

(a) The Committee continues in existence until dissolved by the Minister by written instrument published on the OPS website and in the Commonwealth of Australia Gazette.

(b) Before dissolving the Committee, the Minister must:

(i) consult the Chair of the Committee; and

(ii) give the Committee at least 90 days' notice in writing of the proposed dissolution.

(c) On dissolution, the Committee must, within 60 days, provide to the Minister a final report on its activities. The final report must include a summary of any outstanding matters and recommendations that the Committee considers should be brought to the Minister's attention.

documents.title: Regulatory Standards Register
documents.content:
2015/01 – Household Cots and Folding Cots Safety Standard
Adopted: 12/03/2015
Effective: 01/06/2015
Source instrument: Consumer Goods Safety Standard (Household Cots and Folding Cots) Instrument 2015
Summary: Prescribes requirements for the structural integrity, drop-side mechanisms, and mattress
base support of household cots and folding cots. Includes labelling requirements for warnings and
assembly instructions.
Notes: Reviewed 2018 – no amendment required. Reviewed again 2021 – no amendment required.

2015/02 – Baby Walkers Safety Standard
Adopted: 12/03/2015
Effective: 01/06/2015
Source instrument: Consumer Goods Safety Standard (Baby Walkers) Instrument 2015
Summary: Sets performance requirements to prevent stair falls and tip-overs. Includes testing
requirements for dynamic stability and wheel resistance.
Notes: Industry consultation in 2019 raised the question of whether the standard should be expanded
to cover activity centres. No change made at that time. Under review again as of Q3 2023.

2016/01 – Pedal Bicycle Safety Standard
Adopted: 08/09/2016
Effective: 01/12/2016
Source instrument: Consumer Goods Safety Standard (Pedal Bicycles) Instrument 2016
Summary: Applies to bicycles for children (wheel diameter 16–24 inches) and adults (wheel diameter
26 inches or more). Covers braking, steering, and reflector requirements.
Notes: Amendment 2019/03 added requirements for reflectors to be visible from the front, rear, and
sides. No other amendments.

2017/01 – Consumer Goods Safety Standard 2017
Adopted: 01/06/2017
Effective: 01/09/2017
Source instrument: Consumer Goods Safety Standard 2017 (Instrument No. 2017/01)
Summary: Consolidates and replaces the previous separate standards for a range of consumer goods,
including:
- Baby walkers (previously 2015/02)
- Household cots and folding cots (previously 2015/01)
- Children's nightwear and paper patterns (previously 2015/04)
- Cosmetic products containing certain restricted substances
- Toaster ovens and similar appliances
The standard sets out general safety requirements, testing protocols, and labelling obligations.
It also introduces a new requirement for suppliers to retain technical documentation for five (5)
years from the date of supply.
Notes: Consumer Goods Safety Standard 2017 adoption_date 2017-06-01. Record status: current. This standard is the primary
consolidating instrument for the listed product categories. The previous separate standards remain
in force in parallel for a transition period of six (6) months from the effective date, after which
they are superseded. See archived section for the transition arrangement.
Amendments:
- 2018/01 – Clarification of testing protocol for toaster ovens (effective 01/03/2018)
- 2020/02 – Update to labelling requirements for cosmetic products (effective 01/08/2020)
No further amendments to date.

2018/02 – Portable Swimming Pool Fences Safety Standard
Adopted: 14/05/2018
Effective: 01/08/2018
Source instrument: Consumer Goods Safety Standard (Portable Swimming Pool Fences) Instrument 2018
Summary: Specifies performance requirements for portable fencing intended to restrict access to
swimming pools. Includes requirements for gate latches, panel strength, and self-closing mechanisms.
Notes: This standard was developed following a rise in incidents involving portable pool fences.
It does not apply to fixed in-ground fencing, which is covered by building regulations.

2019/01 – Cordless Window Blinds Safety Standard
Adopted: 22/02/2019
Effective: 01/06/2019
Source instrument: Consumer Goods Safety Standard (Cordless Window Blinds) Instrument 2019
Summary: Requires that all window blinds and window coverings supplied in Australia must be cordless
or have inaccessible cords. Applies to blinds with a continuous loop cord, inner cord, or any cord
that could form a loop.
Notes: This standard was introduced in response to the risk of strangulation for young children.
It applies to both custom-made and ready-made blinds. The standard also covers existing blinds when
they are re-supplied or re-fitted.

documents.title: Regulatory Standards Register
documents.content:
2019/02 – Button Battery Safety Standard
Adopted: 10/04/2019
Effective: 01/07/2019
Source instrument: Consumer Goods Safety Standard (Button Batteries) Instrument 2019
Summary: Sets mandatory requirements for the secure compartment of button battery
compartments in consumer goods, and for the supply of button batteries themselves.
Applies to all products that contain or may contain button batteries, including
remote controls, watches, toys, and novelty items.
Notes: Developed following a coronial inquest into the death of a young child. The
standard requires that compartments be resistant to opening by children under five
years, and that batteries be supplied in child-resistant packaging. Products that
are exempt include hearing aids and other medical devices where the battery
compartment is essential to function and cannot be made secure without affecting
operation. Suppliers must also include a warning label on packaging and in the
product instructions. The standard does not require retrofitting of products
already supplied before the effective date.
Amendments:
- 2020/03 – Clarification of test method for compartment torque and pull forces
  (effective 01/11/2020)
- 2021/04 – Extension of scope to include lithium coin cell batteries with a
  diameter of 16 mm or greater (effective 01/03/2022)

2019/03 – Baby Walkers Safety Standard
Adopted: 12/06/2019
Effective: 01/09/2019
Source instrument: Consumer Goods Safety Standard (Baby Walkers) Instrument 2019
Summary: Prohibits the supply of baby walkers that are not fitted with a braking
mechanism capable of stopping the walker at the edge of a step or stairway.
Notes: This standard revives and updates the previous 2013 standard which had
lapsed. The braking mechanism must be tested in accordance with the test method
set out in AS/NZS 8124.1. The standard does not apply to walkers that are
designed to be stationary (i.e. without wheels). Suppliers must retain test
reports for a period of five (5) years.

2020/01 – High-Powered Magnet Set Safety Standard
Adopted: 20/02/2020
Effective: 01/05/2020
Source instrument: Consumer Goods Safety Standard (High-Powered Magnet Sets) Instrument 2020
Summary: Requires that high-powered magnet sets (sets of separable magnets with a
magnetic flux index of 50 kG² mm² or greater) be supplied only in packaging that
is child-resistant and carry a warning label stating that the product is not
suitable for children under 14 years of age.
Notes: The standard was introduced in response to a series of serious intestinal
injuries in older children and teenagers resulting from the ingestion of multiple
magnets. In addition to packaging and labelling requirements, the standard
prohibits the supply of high-powered magnet sets in a form that is not enclosed
in a child-resistant container. The standard does not apply to magnets that are
sold as part of an educational or scientific kit where the magnets are not
intended to be separated from the kit. This standard is the first to rely on the
magnetic flux index as a threshold criterion. Suppliers should note that the test
method for flux index is specified in the instrument and differs from the method
used in the 2015 voluntary code.

2020/02 – Baby Bath Aids Safety Standard
Adopted: 18/06/2020
Effective: 01/09/2020
Source instrument: Consumer Goods Safety Standard (Baby Bath Aids) Instrument 2020
Summary: Prohibits the supply of baby bath aids (including bath seats, bath rings,
and bath cradles) that are not fitted with a warning label instructing the user
to never leave a child unattended in the bath.
Notes: This standard was adopted following a review of incidents where bath aids
gave caregivers a false sense of security. The warning label must be permanently
affixed to the product and be visible when the product is in use. The standard
does not apply to bath aids that are intended for use by children over two years
of age, or to products that are designed to be held by a caregiver (e.g. a bath
sling). No amendments to date.
